slides.texte_overlay:
How to stop feeling awkward
at the gym (and finally relax)
Go with a written plan. Four exercises, sets and reps on your phone. Knowing exactly what you'll do next stops the wandering around that makes you feel everyone is watching you.
Remember nobody is looking at you. Everyone is focused on their own set, their own music, their own reflection. The gym is the one place where people care least about you.
Start at quieter hours. Early morning or mid-afternoon. Fewer people means less pressure, and by the time you go at peak hours, the machines already feel familiar.
Ask someone how a machine works. "Sorry, how do you set this one up?" Regulars love helping, and that one question often turns a stranger into a friendly face you see every week.
Learn basic gym manners. Wipe the bench, rerack the weights, don't sit on a machine scrolling. Knowing the unwritten rules removes the fear of doing something wrong.
Track your progress. Write down every weight you lift. Watching the numbers go up week after week builds a quiet confidence that no amount of positive thinking can match.
Try this for 30 days: five minutes a day of history, art or science between sets. A busy, curious mind leaves less room for the worry that everyone is judging you.
